_meta.note: Weights are relative, not required to sum to 1 — the scorer normalizes them. Hard filters run before scoring and are absolute.
_meta.stock_note: `exclude_stock: ["out"]` is a filter and not a scoring penalty on purpose. A plan nobody can buy is not a cheap plan, it is not a plan, and no weighting should be able to average that away. `unknown` is deliberately allowed through — most rows were never checked, and silently dropping them would be a bigger distortion than admitting the gap. The report says which rows were checked.

jod.label: Jod orchestrator (stated goal)
jod.description: Free to do anything, good availability, good internet access, good location coverage, cheapest. Weighted in the order the goal was stated.

verified.label: Jod weighting, verified rows only
verified.description: Same weights as `jod`, restricted to rows whose price was read off the standing catalogue and whose order path was actually opened. Every row checked on 2026-08-09 turned out to be wrong in the original dataset, so an unverified row outranking a verified one is not evidence that it is better — only that nobody has looked yet. This profile is the defensible answer; `jod` is the optimistic one.

cheapest.label: Pure cost
cheapest.description: Sanity check: what wins if only price matters. Used to show what the balanced model is trading away.

freedom.label: Maximum permissiveness
freedom.description: Sanity check: what wins if only 'free to do anything' matters.

production.label: Reliability-first
production.description: Sanity check: what wins if Jod must not go down, cost secondary.

fx_to_usd._note: Update these before trusting absolute dollar figures. Rates are the single biggest source of drift in this dataset.
